newsitem.title: UK: Airtours, Carnival to buy Costa line.
newsitem.headline: Airtours, Carnival to buy Costa line.

text.p: British-based holiday operator Airtours Plc and its U.S. cruise partner Carnival Corp. said Thursday they signed a letter of intent with the main owners of Italian cruise line Costa Crociere SpA to buy the company.

The two prospective purchasers said they expected to launch a joint tender offer that would make them 50-50 owners of Costa and expected to pay about 452 billion lire, or 181 million pounds ($301 million) in total.

Costa Crociere, based in Genoa, claims to be Europe's largest cruise company, with 10 ships. In the year ended 1995, the latest for which figures were available, it had profit before taxes of about 18.2 million pounds ($30.3 million) on revenues of about 308 million pounds ($513 million).
"Both Airtours and Carnival intend to meet their share of the offer out of existing resources or lines of credit," the companies said in a statement.

Carnival and Airtours formed a strategic alliance in March, combining the might of the world's largest cruise line operator with one of the largest air holiday operators, with Carnival taking a near 30 percent stake in the British firm.
